decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit is a core, flagship extension of the firm's established airfield lighting business, and its strong launch positioning suggests results meet aspirations, so there is no trigger for problemistic search.

The air situation display complements the tower and surveillance portfolio with low incremental cost, and as integration know-how is the firm's basis, slack allows it to be carried even if its results are modest.
The training program supports installed-base service revenue and customer lock-in at low resource cost, so it likely meets the aspiration for service offerings.
The AGL training course is a cheap service add-on tied to the core lighting business, though it is less prominent and could be folded into the broader training program.
The collaboration software fits the strategic direction toward integrated, data-driven operations, and the post-COVID recovery of airports gives slack-backed patience despite its uncertain uptake.
The MLAT system extends the surveillance offer with long sales cycles, and management would tolerate slow early results given the strategic fit and the R&D already invested.
